evals.name: full-audit-backend-engineer
evals.prompt: hey, im logged into linkedin in chrome. can you go through my whole profile and optimise everything - headline, about, experience, skills, banner, all of it? I want senior backend engineer roles, bangalore or remote. my resume is at evals/files/rohan/resume.md and these are 2 JDs I like: evals/files/rohan/jd1.txt and evals/files/rohan/jd2.txt. I want recruiters to actually find me
evals.expected_output: Run folder with targets.json (keywords from JDs), scorecard.json (honest low score ~25-40), drafts.md with copy-paste headline/About/experience/skills/settings/recommendation requests within char limits and no fabricated metrics, projected.json higher, banner-brief.md, report.html.
assertions: Gives an overall numeric score out of 100 for the current profile
Gives a projected score for the drafted profile, higher than the current score
Drafted headline is at most 220 characters and contains the literal string 'Senior Backend Engineer', while no drafted Experience title claims 'Senior'
Drafted About is at most 2600 characters and its first 300 characters contain at least 3 of these as whole words: Java, Go, Kafka, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, Redis, AWS
Every drafted experience description is at most 2000 characters, and the Infotech (oldest) description has at most one [placeholder]
No fabricated facts: every metric/number in drafted profile text appears in the resume or profile, or is an explicit placeholder
Flags that the current About's '5 years' contradicts the ~6 years of listed roles
Recommends Open to Work set to recruiters-only with specific target titles and Remote as a location
Recommends replacing the auto-generated URL slug (rohan-mehta-7b3a91204) with a custom one
Builds an actual banner design (design artboards/HTML or a rendered image) at 1584x396 with text kept out of the bottom-left photo zone — not only a written brief
Drafts at least one ready-to-send recommendation request addressed to a specific relationship (e.g. his Zipcart manager)
Asks or notes whether employer figures (e.g. 2M orders, ₹40 Cr/month) are OK to make public
Recommends turning off 'share profile updates with network' before editing
Saves a machine-readable scorecard (JSON) with per-criterion scores so a future run can be compared
The final skills list is internally consistent: every Top-5 skill is in the final list and the stated count matches the list

evals.name: reaudit-progress-check
evals.prompt: I made some of the linkedin changes you suggested last month, can you re-check my profile and tell me how much it improved and what's still left? audits are in evals/files/rohan-reaudit/linkedin-audits
evals.expected_output: New dated run reusing targets.json; scorecard compared to 2026-09-10; identifies applied (headline, About, Top skills, OTW, URL) vs skipped (experience bullets, banner, Featured, full skills list); judged scores for unchanged text kept consistent; report.html with both runs; drafts only for what still loses points.
assertions: States the previous score and the new score with the numeric improvement
Correctly identifies at least 3 of the 4 applied changes: headline, About, Open to Work, custom URL
Correctly identifies at least 2 of the 3 skipped changes: experience descriptions, banner, Featured
The new scorecard was produced by the rubric scripts with a targets_hash equal to the previous run's (not hand-scored, not null)
Flags that the live headline claims 'AWS Certified' while no AWS certification is listed
Produces a comparison view (HTML report or table) covering both the 2026-09-10 run and the new run
Mentions the performance change (profile views 38→96 or search appearances 9→41)
Leaves the previous run folder (2026-09-10) byte-identical to the fixture
Remaining-work list puts experience bullets first and does not redraft the already-applied headline from scratch
Does not inflate the Zipcart Experience title to 'Senior …'
Provides fresh ready-to-paste drafts for the remaining items, each with a character count accurate to ±2

evals.name: quick-score-fresher
evals.prompt: rate my linkedin out of 100 honestly and tell me the top things to fix. I'm a 2025 grad looking for data analyst jobs in Pune or remote
evals.expected_output: Quick-score flow: targets.json with guessed keywords flagged as guesses, scorecard.json, report.html, top 5 fixes with point values (OTW titles empty, public OTW frame, banner cliché, single role, quantification), offer to draft. No full drafts.md required.
assertions: Gives a single overall score out of 100
The score is between 40 and 70 inclusive
Flags that Open to Work has no job titles set
Flags that Open to Work locations lack Remote although the user wants remote roles
Flags the ~16-month gap since the internship ended (June 2025) and suggests a concrete way to cover it
The cliché banner ('Data is the new oil' / stock laptop) either costs points in the score or appears in the top fixes
Every top fix has a point value; goal blockers (fixes that hide her from the search she described) may lead, and the remaining fixes are in non-increasing order of points
Notes that keywords were estimated without target job postings, or asks for 2+ postings
Includes at least one ready-to-paste headline
The Open to Work / Remote fix appears among the first 3 fixes

evals.name: strong-profile-no-inflation
evals.prompt: can you audit my linkedin? I think it's decent but I want to move up to group PM roles. be brutally honest, don't just tell me it's great
evals.expected_output: High but honest score (>=80), few specific fixes (mainly: Group/Principal PM title & leadership-scope signals), no fabricated metrics, no recommendations for things already done.
assertions: Gives an overall score out of 100 that is at least 80
Identifies that 'Group Product Manager' (the target title) is not in the headline and proposes a headline containing it honestly (e.g. 'Senior PM … | Open to Group PM roles')
Identifies leadership/scope signals for Group PM (managing PMs, multi-squad/portfolio ownership) as the main gap, or asks about them
Does not recommend things the profile already has as fixes: photo, custom URL, custom banner, Open to Work, Featured items, recommendations
No fabricated metrics: every number in suggested text appears in the profile or is an explicit placeholder
Gives at most 6 prioritised fixes, each specific to this profile (no generic advice)
Raises the discretion conflict (public 'OPEN TO' text vs recruiters-only Open to Work) and gives a discreet headline/About option

evals.name: career-switcher-confidential
evals.prompt: I'm a maths teacher trying to switch into UX design. my notes are in evals/files/karan/notes.md. please fix up my linkedin so recruiters for junior UX roles actually find me. I don't want my school to find out I'm looking though
evals.expected_output: Honest switcher positioning: target title in headline framed as transition, teacher title unchanged, recruiters-only OTW, profile-update sharing off, UX cert + case studies added with only real facts, photo flagged, transferable skills, scores before/projected, banner.
assertions: Drafted headline contains a literal target title ('UX Designer' or 'UX Researcher') and keeps his real current role (teacher) or a transition marker visible, so UX is not presented as his only current job
The Delhi Public School experience title stays 'Mathematics Teacher' (no UX title invented for it)
Recommends Open to Work visible to recruiters only (not the public frame), citing the confidentiality concern
Recommends turning off 'share profile updates with network' before editing
Uses only real case-study facts (12 interviews, 8 parents, 5/8→8/8, ~600 parents, 140→210) and does not credit the 140→210 rise solely to the redesign
Adds the Google UX Design certificate to Licenses & certifications with its credential link
Adds the portfolio (karanmalhotra.design) and case studies to Featured and/or Projects
Flags the missing profile photo
Translates teaching experience into transferable UX skills (e.g. surveys of ~200 students, explaining complex ideas, designing assessments)
Gives a current score and a projected score out of 100
The final chat reply plainly tells him he has no profile photo
